content.content: clause by clause, against the two recorded prerequisites: (1) licence - no element of the decision contradicts wzsxvmvw or yqwsztww; fail on each contradicting element, naming that element and the prerequisite it contradicts. (2) one move - the viewport consequence the decision puts behind the selection the recorded key presses make is the centring move wzsxvmvw records, carried with that move's recorded terms: which axis term applies and what it requires there, whether a recorded pan limit reaches the move, and the zoom level left unchanged; fail where the decision states a second move, a pan, zoom or clamp rule of its own, a per-axis or limit term that diverges from the recorded ones, or a viewport consequence the recorded move does not carry. (3) the centred node - a move so triggered centres on the node the recorded selection identifies; fail where it centres on any other node, or where which node is centred is settled by a rule the record does not state. (4) the trigger stands on its own - the centring takes the selection those key presses make as its trigger and hinges on no recorded centring trigger (focus arriving on a node, an activation of an id a relationship section lists) and on no property of that selection the record does not state; fail where an element makes the centring depend on either recorded trigger, narrows or widens either to reach this selection, or assumes a property of the selection that no prerequisite records. (5) the selection stays its own decision's - which key presses act, in which context, over which set of nodes, in which direction, in which order and with which wrap are yqwsztww's as recorded, and the matters it leaves to the decisions it names stay with them: what marks a node, what the recorded order is, what the same key press does outside the search field, and that marking selects nothing by itself; fail where the decision restates, narrows, widens, substitutes or newly settles any of them. Accept any recorded phrasing that puts the viewport consequence on the recorded move, the centred node on the recorded selection and the selection on its own decision; no implementation of the selection or of the centring is required.
content.rationale: both endpoints are inline statements read as their own form: the evaluated decision is an inline requirement, wzsxvmvw is an inline EARS requirement and yqwsztww is an inline EARS requirement, so both edges sit in the structured-to-structured cell, for which the eval-matrix has no entry - the default cell applies, the gate form of evals/natural-to-natural.md, and that gap stays flagged for a matrix entry. The use is a fan-out over two prerequisites that one clause-by-clause non-violation review decides: wzsxvmvw states the centring move and the terms it is carried with, and yqwsztww states the selection the two key presses in the search field make, so one subject checked against those two is one review, while a second evaluation of the same subject against the same two prerequisites would either restate this one or drift from it. The criterion cites the recorded move and the recorded selection rather than restating either, because the axis and limit terms and the centred-node rule are wzsxvmvw's own and the keys, the acted-on set, the order and the wrap are yqwsztww's: a copy of either would track its wording, break under its rewording, and could not tell a cited rule from one settled anew. No clause names an element of the evaluated decision in advance, so the criterion survives that decision being reworded without changing what it decides; a reviewer applies it by reading the three recorded nodes and reporting the element at issue, and there is nothing to run.
